KEY FINDINGS
NYC's deployed congestion-pricing program shows real bus and subway
ridership gains, but the demand shift is spatially uneven across the city.
Free bus schemes for women in India causally raise workforce
participation, with the largest gains in the most mobility-restricted districts.
A new continental-scale routing algorithm (T-REX) answers transit
queries across all of Europe in under 10 milliseconds.
PAPER OF THE DAY
Public transit gains and spatially uneven travel demand
changes after NYC congestion pricing
Donghang Li, Dingyi Zhuang, Yunlin Li, Chenan Shen, Nina Cao, Yunhan Zheng, Shenhao Wang, Jinhua Zhao
Time-series foundation models build calibrated counterfactual demand forecasts for NYC's January
2025 cordon congestion-pricing program. Real post-policy bus and subway ridership gains are found,
but the shift in travel demand is spatially uneven — some corridors absorb far more change than
others, showing congestion pricing's transit effects can't be modeled as a single city-wide average.
EMERGING THEMES
Congestion pricing moves
from theory to live policy
laboratory

High

ACTIONABLE TAKEAWAYS
Cities evaluating congestion pricing can cite NYC's deployed program as real-world evidence of
transit ridership gains, but should plan for spatially uneven demand shifts.
Gender-targeted transit subsidies work primarily by easing non-financial mobility constraints,
with the largest gains in the most mobility-restricted populations.
15-minute-city planners should audit whether new radial transit lines actually improve
peripheral amenity access, not just social-mixing potential.
Pairing free public transit with AMoD permits is a more effective equity lever than regulating
AMoD pricing or service areas alone.
Continental-scale routing platforms should evaluate T-REX-style multi-level overlay routing
over unindexed or simple trip-based approaches.
